tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Edit the freytag-forge repo checkout at /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge directly (absolute paths; no worktree). Do NOT git commit, push, or touch .git. Everything you write is offline and hermetic: no model call, no network.

OWNED FILES (create these; edit nothing else): scripts/ringer/affordance/invitation_report.py and tests/test_invitation_report.py. READ-ONLY reuse: scripts/ringer/affordance/cue_eligibility_compare.py and sibling_reachability.py (import their helpers: _scene_states, _matching_reveals, _cue_fact_ids, _state, _apply_reveal, _seed_reveal_state, _activate_unfired_storylets), storygame/runtime/reveal_eligibility.py (explain_reveal), storygame/runtime/candidate_matcher.py (uniquely_matched_candidate / _matches_all: the real matcher).

GOAL: a small INVITATION REPORT for the Continuity Initiative story package (data/stories/continuity-initiative). It is a REPORT, not an acceptance gate: it never fails because of what it finds, matching and spending are unchanged, and it must not touch the loader or runtime.

DEFINITION: an invitation is player-visible text that gives a reasonable expectation that acting on a named person, place or thing produces a meaningful response. This version covers cue_text only (each delivery's `cue_text` in handoffs.yaml). For every scene and every state that cue_eligibility_compare._scene_states yields, where the cue is shown (the delivery's cue fact is not already true and RuntimeEngine._cue_reveal_available says available, using the same SimpleNamespace call as cue_eligibility_compare._cue_available), record one row:
- scene, state label (the path to that state, e.g. 'entry' or 'after SL-1C-C through k_sl_1c_c_r2'), delivery fact id, the cue_text;
- the reveals that establish the cue fact (_matching_reveals) with explain_reveal(...).reason for each ('eligible' when explain_reveal says eligible);
- for each eligible reveal, a REPRESENTATIVE COMMAND built from the reveal's own action_evidence groups (take the first phrase of each group, join with spaces, written as a plain imperative: use the first word of each group exactly, no first person) and whether the real matcher (uniquely_matched_candidate or the equivalent used by the engine; read candidate_matcher.py) selects exactly that reveal for it in that state;
- a label: 'eligible response' (some matching reveal is eligible AND the representative command matches exactly it); 'unanswered invitation' (cue shown but no matching reveal is eligible, i.e. every one is spent, established, prerequisite_missing or inactive, and not hidden); 'unknown' (no matching reveal found at all, or the command did not match uniquely, or any other case you cannot classify). Do NOT use 'withdrawn' or 'ordinary action - review' for rows you cannot establish; those two labels are listed in the legend but only the human reviewer assigns them. Skip reveals whose audience.kind is world_only (the existing helper already does).
Also print a short LIMITS section: it covers cue_text only, only the states cue_eligibility_compare covers (not exhaustive), it cannot see narrator-invented pointers, and delivery pointer lines and entry text are NOT scored: list them instead as an UNREVIEWED CANDIDATES section = every sentence in the package's delivery fallback/delivery texts and scene entry texts that contains a pointing phrase (examples: 'is worth', 'may be worth', 'waits', 'lies beside', 'ready to answer', 'overlooks', 'closing in') with its source id, so a human can build the invitation-to-action mapping. Print them verbatim, unscored.
Output plain text to stdout from main(argv) -> int returning 0; `uv`-free: it must run as `.venv/bin/python -m scripts.ringer.affordance.invitation_report` from the repo root (follow how cue_eligibility_compare.py is invoked).

TESTS (tests/test_invitation_report.py): (1) the report runs and returns 0 and prints the legend and LIMITS section; (2) every row carries one of the labels 'eligible response', 'unanswered invitation', 'unknown'; (3) after the cue change on main there are 0 'unanswered invitation' rows for cues whose reveal is spent (assert the count of spent-reveal rows equals 0, citing cue_eligibility_compare's CUE_SHOWN_BUT_SPENT count of 0); (4) at least one 'eligible response' row exists for the 1A drawer cue (delivery memory_card_recovered or whichever fact the 1A cue_text belongs to; find it in handoffs.yaml). Keep tests fast.

HOW TO RUN (sandbox cannot run uv): PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_invitation_report.py ; run the report once: PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m scripts.ringer.affordance.invitation_report | tail -60 ; ruff via the same interpreter: -m ruff check --fix . and -m ruff format . (only your two files may change). Finish by replying with the label counts the report printed.
tasks.check: cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && bad=$(git status --short | grep -v -E 'scripts/ringer/affordance/invitation_report.py|tests/test_invitation_report.py' || true); [ -z "$bad" ] || { echo FAIL outside owned files:; echo "$bad"; exit 1; }; test -f scripts/ringer/affordance/invitation_report.py && test -f tests/test_invitation_report.py || { echo FAIL missing files; exit 1; }; out=$(PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python -m scripts.ringer.affordance.invitation_report) || { echo FAIL report crashed; exit 1; }; echo "$out" | tail -40; echo "$out" | grep -qi 'limits' || { echo FAIL no LIMITS section; exit 1; }; echo "$out" | grep -q 'eligible response' || { echo FAIL no eligible-response rows; exit 1; }; echo "$out" | grep -qi 'unreviewed' || { echo FAIL no unreviewed candidates section; exit 1; }; TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n auto 2>&1 | tail -4; .venv/bin/python -m ruff check . && .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check . && echo PASS
tasks.verified: the report runs offline, prints labelled rows, a limits section and unreviewed candidates, tests and ruff pass, only the two owned files changed
